@copilot Update this PR directly with these two focused simplifications, preserving its caller-context restoration behavior.

In instrumentation/rocketmq/rocketmq-client-4.8/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/rocketmqclient/v4_8/RocketMqProducerWrapper.java, pass parentContext directly to SendState.wrap, for example state.wrap((SendCallback) args[callbackIndex], parentContext), and let the anonymous SendCallback capture the method parameter. Remove the parentContext field from SendState and its constructor parameter and assignment. Keep producer completion before application callback invocation and keep the explicit try-with-resources scopes around both delegate callbacks. Preserve null-callback behavior.

In instrumentation/rocketmq/rocketmq-client-4.8/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/rocketmqclient/v4_8/AbstractRocketMqBatchCallbackTest.java, replace callbackModes()'s four nested streams and exhaustive 16-case boolean product with a smaller explicit, named scenario table using Arguments.argumentSet(...). Keep core inline/deferred success/failure coverage plus focused no-caller-span and throwing-callback scenarios. Cover throwing success and failure callbacks in both inline and deferred execution, without exhaustively crossing every independent dimension. Keep the real DefaultMQProducer batch API and encoding path, the shared library/javaagent fixture and separate concrete test entry points, the unrelated completion-thread context, the custom context marker, producer-ended-before-callback assertions, and restoration of the previous context even when a callback throws. Preserve trace assertions for both message-create-span modes.

Do not introduce a shared production callback abstraction just to deduplicate the short scope blocks. Do not change callback semantics or add before-send-hook work. Limit changes to these simplifications and directly necessary adjustments. Run the relevant targeted callback tests for library and javaagent instrumentation, including the existing javaagent create-spans-disabled variant, using the repository's formatting and validation guidance.

replies.body: Applied in commit `f319f747`. The callback wrapper now captures the supplied caller context, and the shared test uses 10 named scenarios. The targeted library, javaagent, and create-spans-disabled callback tests and formatting checks pass.

@copilot Update this PR directly to simplify callback-context coverage into real broker-backed tests in the existing AbstractRocketMqClientTest. The user prefers simpler real-world tests over exhaustive coverage of every timing and exception nuance. This supersedes the earlier request to retain the controlled callback scenario matrix.

Reuse instrumentation/rocketmq/rocketmq-client-4.8/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/rocketmqclient/v4_8/AbstractRocketMqClientTest.java and its existing broker, producer, and consumer setup. Its testRocketmqProduceCallback() already sends a single Message through SendCallback but does not assert the callback's context. Add focused callback-context coverage through the normal single-message and batch send APIs, preferably as a small parameterized test if the same expectations apply. Send under a caller context, create a span inside the application callback, and verify that the callback span has the caller as parent rather than the producer send span. Keep complete, appropriate telemetry assertions for library and installed-javaagent runs and the existing create-spans-disabled variant.

Replace and remove the synthetic AbstractRocketMqBatchCallbackTest and both new RocketMqBatchCallbackTest subclasses under library/src/test and javaagent/src/test. Avoid reflective transport replacement, custom synthetic completion-thread fixtures, and the exhaustive inline/deferred/failure/throwing matrix. Preserve the current production callback-scoping fix and the previous simplification that captures parentContext directly in SendState.wrap. Do not add before-send-hook work or unrelated production changes.

Before discarding the existing regression fixture, verify that the replacement real batch test genuinely detects the bug: temporarily remove the relevant callback context scopes without committing that temporary change, confirm the new regression test fails, restore the production fix, and confirm it passes. Check the relevant library and installed-javaagent paths; generic executor context propagation can mask this defect, so a passing real send alone is not enough evidence. If a straightforward real test cannot reproduce the defect, report the concrete evidence rather than silently deleting effective regression coverage or adding another elaborate fixture. If the single-message case reveals a separate pre-existing context-propagation gap, report it rather than weakening the expected contract or broadening this PR's production fix.

Account for RocketMQ swallowing callback exceptions: communicate callback assertion failures back to the test thread through the existing future or another simple repository-standard mechanism, with bounded waits. Follow repository formatting and targeted-validation guidance. Run the relevant callback tests in library and javaagent modes, including the existing create-spans-disabled variant, and retain concise evidence of the fail-without-fix and pass-with-fix runs.

replies.body: Committed as `bead301c`. Replaced the synthetic fixture with a shared broker-backed batch callback test and removed the synthetic subclasses. With callback scopes temporarily removed, the regression failed in library, javaagent, and create-spans-disabled runs; restoring the scopes made all three pass. A real single-message callback also showed a separate existing caller-context propagation gap in both library and javaagent modes, so I kept this change batch-scoped and did not broaden production behavior. The targeted test tasks and `spotlessCheck` pass.

threads.body: [Testing] This regression checks only successful completion with a caller span and does not force inline completion, leaving failure-callback scoping and spanless-caller restoration unverified. Add focused cases through the library wrapper and installed-agent paths for inline completion and for failure with a spanless caller while an unrelated completion span is current. Assert the captured context, callback-created span parentage, and restoration of the completion context after the callback returns; extend the existing inline mock and captured-executor tests where applicable.

replies.body: Keeping the focused broker-backed regression here. It checks the captured caller context and callback span parentage, and removing the callback scopes makes it fail in library, installed-agent, and create-spans-disabled runs. We deliberately dropped synthetic inline, failure, and spanless-completion cases in favor of simpler real-world coverage, so I'm not restoring that matrix.
